newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Wedgwood says on track for goals.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Wedgwood says on track for goals.

text.p: Irish fine china and crystal group Waterford Wedgwood Plc said on Wednesday that it was on track to meet its objectives despite challenging times.
"The 1996 results very clearly illustrate the robust financial progress being made at Waterford Wedgwood," Chairman, Tony O'Reilly said in a statement.

"The turnaround is clearly complete with sales growth in double digits for the past two years and a return on sales that's broken 10 percent for the first time since Waterford and Wedgwood became one."
O'Reilly told shareholders at an annual meeting that the group was on track to meet its targets in 1997.

"Certainly these are challenging times. While trading is proving difficult for our Japanese-orientated business, as the current yen rate coupled with the strength of sterling bites into international tourism, the ongoing strength of our U.S. business proves the capability of Waterford Wedgwood to cope with regional fluctuations," O'Reilly said.
The chairman told shareholders that consistent with its growth and positioning strategy, Waterford had raised its stake to approximately 25 percent in Rosenthal A.G..
Waterford Wedgwood still has options over a further 13.6 percent of the enlarged equity after Rosenthal's recent rights issue, it said.
